name: Caribbean Dominoes
description: Caribbean dominoes: draw/block game, double-six. Four players in partnerships; play to empty hand or block. Regional rules vary (Jamaican, Haitian, etc).

overview.description: Caribbean dominoes: draw/block game, double-six. Four players in partnerships; play to empty hand or block. Regional rules vary (Jamaican, Haitian, etc).

history.origins: Domino games are enthusiastically played on many Caribbean islands. Typically the style of play is boisterous, and the pieces are slammed down on the table rather than placed gently. Most often there are four players in fixed partnerships. The rules vary from place to place; often the objective is for one team to win several rounds in a row (e.g. 4 or 6), which is characteristic of the Caribbean. Regional variants are documented for Jamaica (Partner and Cut Throat), Haiti, Puerto Rico (Chiva), and Cuba.
timeline: Early 21st century: Played across Caribbean islands in partnership style; regional variants in Jamaica, Haiti, Cuba, Puerto Rico.

rules.objective: Win each round by being the first team to play all tiles (empty hand), or when the game is blocked, have the lowest total spots on unplayed tiles. Win a set number of rounds in a row (e.g. 4 or 6) to win the match.
rules.gameplay: 7 tiles each (4p). Highest double leads. Match ends; if can't play draw from boneyard. Pass when blocked. First team empty or lowest at block wins.
